chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

'When you attend to the dying person before he dies, prompt him with the testimony that there is no god except Allah, Alone, with no partner for Him, and that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger.'

key_terms.الْمَيِّت: The dying person (literally 'the dead/dying one') — used here for one approaching death, not yet deceased
key_terms.شَهَادَة: Testimony/Declaration of faith — the shahada, the foundational creed of Islam
key_terms.لَقِّنْهُ: Prompt him/Instruct him to say — from talqeen, the act of prompting a dying person to recite the shahada

ai.seo_question: What should you say to a dying Muslim? What is talqeen in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) instructs that those present at a person's deathbed should prompt the dying person to recite the shahada — the declaration that Allah is One and Muhammad is His Messenger. This practice, known as talqeen, is a recommended act aimed at ensuring the dying person's last words affirm Islamic monotheism. In early Islamic jurisprudence, dying with the shahada on one's lips was considered a mark of a blessed death and a sign of firm faith.
